genre: creator educator/promo reel (the corpus's dominant family — 7 of 16)
identity: A credible speaker and one clear argument form the spine. Visual energy can come from performance, framing, selective speech-synced typography, specific proof, graphic props, cutaways or deliberate stillness. The system responds to rhetorical structure and the brief rather than imposing a cut rate, numbered-list template or generic CTA. Detailed exemplar skin: kinetic-typography-talking-head.json.

bright-kinetic.notes: cream canvas, matted subject, red display sections, words orbit the speaker — see kinetic-typography-talking-head.json

dark-minimal.notes: moody room, tiny captions, full-screen GRAPHIC INTERLUDES (floating panels, progress bars, title cards) between talking spans

dark-maximalist.notes: 3D slab/neon type, comic sunburst radials behind the subject, prop gags (framed self-portrait), metaphor b-roll interludes, whip transitions, ONE accent (red or yellow)

walking-pitch.notes: walking toward camera through a location; floating photo-collage props fan out beside the walker; gauge graphics for numbers; neon logo outro

filmmaker-street.notes: giant condensed LABELS name each demo shot (WIDE / 70MM MEDIUM / 135MM CLOSE UP); app-UI demo segments on grid-paper background; word cards (TIME, MONEY)

resource-cards.notes: pinned title card through the hook; N item cards on a fixed template (cover + title + view-count ladder animating up); blurred list tease behind the speaker; comment-keyword pill

shared_rules.spine: let the credible speaker and argument remain the spine; cut or reframe when meaning, energy, evidence or composition changes, not at a timer
shared_rules.typography_sync: on-screen words arrive with the thought they clarify; placement uses measured negative space and never covers the face. Not every spoken word needs designed type when captions or performance already carry it
shared_rules.sections: announce only real rhetorical sections. Use display words, title cards, a visual prop, a clean cut or no marker according to the turn; numbered structure belongs only to material that is genuinely a list
shared_rules.props_act_out_claims: when a product action, number or mechanism would be clearer with evidence, show a specific prop that demonstrates it (button clicks, cards count up, photos fan out); do not illustrate obvious connective speech
shared_rules.accent_logic: choose a controlled palette from the footage, brand and brief. One accent is often coherent, but natural color or a deliberate multi-color system can be stronger when the concept earns it
shared_rules.transitions: transitions express a section relationship or movement direction; hard cuts carry ordinary continuity
shared_rules.ending: resolve the promise or land the requested CTA in the final meaningful beat; do not graft a follow/comment card onto material that has no such objective

capability_notes: Same four gaps as the base doc: typography choreography as one composed pass; matte-onto-designed-canvas; UI/graphics prop pack (now also: item-card template with count-up ladder, gauge, progress bar, photo-fan collage); transcript-driven section planning. Everything else exists.
